environment.description: Same application container image deployed on ECS Fargate behind an ALB. The ALB has two relevant configurations: (1) A custom Lambda@Edge function on the associated CloudFront distribution that inspects POST request bodies and rejects requests where any JSON string value exceeds 64 characters or contains parentheses followed by SELECT/UNION/FROM keywords (case-insensitive). (2) The RDS PostgreSQL instance uses a custom pg_hba.conf-equivalent via RDS parameter group with 'rds.restrict_password_commands' enabled, and critically the database role 'webapp_restricted' connects through RDS Proxy which has IAM authentication enforced. The role 'webapp_restricted' has column-level SELECT privileges: GRANT SELECT(id, title, created_at, department, author_id) ON reports TO webapp_restricted; GRANT SELECT(id, username, role) ON users TO webapp_restricted; — no access to password_hash, email, or ssn columns. Additionally, a PostgreSQL security policy (row-level security) is enabled on the reports table with a policy that restricts visibility based on current_setting('app.department'), and the connection initialization runs SET app.department via the RDS Proxy connection initialization query based on IAM role tags.

config.runtime: ECS Fargate, container image identical to exploitable_env
config.distribution: CloudFront with Lambda@Edge viewer-request function (body inspection, 64-char field limit, keyword pattern rejection)
config.load_balancer: ALB with HTTPS listener, forwards to target group on port 3000
config.database: RDS PostgreSQL 15.4 via RDS Proxy with IAM auth
config.rls_policy: Row-level security on reports table, policy uses current_setting('app.department')
config.cloudfront_lambda_edge: Rejects POST bodies with field values >64 chars or matching /\(.*?(select|union|from)/i
